title: Texas franchise tax: the May 15 due date, weekends and holidays, and extensions
rule: The annual franchise tax report is due May 15; an LLC, corporation or limited partnership files its Public Information Report on the same date whether or not it owes tax. A due date falling on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday the Comptroller lists moves to the next day that is none of those. An entity not required to pay by electronic funds transfer (EFT) can extend to November 15 by requesting it by May 15 and paying at least 90 percent of this year's tax or 100 percent of last year's tax if that report was filed by May 14. EFT payers extend to August 15, then November 15.

citation.authority: Tex. Tax Code 111.053, 171.202(b), (c), (e) and (f), and 171.203; 34 Tex. Admin. Code 3.584(i) and 3.585

changeWatch: Amendments to Tax Code 111.053 or 171.202, Comptroller Rules 3.584 and 3.585, and the Comptroller's yearly list of legal holidays published in the Texas Register.

sources.quote: The taxable entity shall file the report before May 16 of each year after the beginning of the regular annual period.

sources.title: Franchise Tax (due dates)
sources.quote: If May 15 falls on a weekend or holiday, the due date will be the next business day.

sources.title: Franchise Tax Extensions of Time to File
sources.quote: Timely means the request is received or postmarked on or before the due date of the original report.
